questions.question: 📞 Sami calls Mina in an emergency: 'I have an 8-year-old child with a fractured permanent tooth! What should I do?' Mina calmly replies: 'First, assess the stage of root development.' Why is this crucial?
options: The stage of development determines the prognosis and treatment technique
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'A tooth with an immature root (open apex) has much better revascularization potential than a mature tooth.' 🦅 Sami: 'I didn't know, thank you Mina!'

questions.question: 🏥 Sami and Mina receive a 10-year-old child with a baby tooth that won't fall out. Sami says: 'It's a persistent baby tooth, let's extract!' Mina replies: 'And the permanent tooth?' What needs to be checked?
options: The presence of the permanent tooth on an X-ray
questions.explanation: 🦅 Sami explains: 'We must first check if the permanent tooth exists and if it is in good position.' 🐆 Mina: 'Sami, you've become cautious!'

questions.question: 🗣️ Sami, during a consultation, tells the parent: 'Your child has a cavity, we need a scaling.' Mina intervenes: 'A scaling in a 5-year-old child?' What is the appropriate treatment?
options: A restoration of the cavity with an age-appropriate material
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'The treatment of a cavity in a child is a restoration, not a scaling.' 🦅 Sami: 'Fine, I'll do a restoration... but quickly!'

questions.question: 🎯 Sami, examining a 6-year-old child, says: 'He has an open bite, it's genetic.' Mina replies: 'Not so sure, look at his thumb-sucking!' What is the link between thumb-sucking and open bite?
options: Prolonged thumb-sucking can create an anterior open bite
questions.explanation: 🦅 Sami explains: 'Thumb-sucking exerts pressure on the incisors, creating an open bite.' 🐆 Mina: 'Sami, you're right!'

questions.question: 📝 Mina reads a file and says: 'The child has amelogenesis imperfecta.' Sami asks: 'How do we treat that?' What are the therapeutic options?
options: Pediatric crowns, aesthetic restoration, tooth protection
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Treatment aims to protect fragile teeth and restore aesthetics.' 🦅 Sami: 'I'll place crowns then!'

questions.question: 🤝 Sami and Mina receive a 9-year-old child with an impacted tooth. Sami says: 'Let's operate immediately!' Mina replies: 'And orthodontics?' What is the recommended sequence?
options: Orthodontic space creation first, then tooth traction
Nothing, it will come out on its own
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Orthodontics creates the necessary space before surgical traction.' 🦅 Sami: 'Fine, we'll do orthodontics first...'

questions.question: 📞 Mina calls Sami: 'I have a 7-year-old child with a bleeding baby tooth after a fall!' Sami replies: 'Let's extract it!' Mina says: 'Not so fast!' What needs to be evaluated?
options: The condition of the underlying permanent tooth
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'We need to evaluate if the permanent tooth is affected or if the baby tooth can be preserved.' 🦅 Sami: 'I'll do an X-ray first.'

questions.question: 🏥 Sami, in an emergency, sees a child with a luxated baby tooth. He says: 'Let's reposition it!' Mina replies: 'No, let's extract it!' What does the literature say?
options: Luxated baby teeth are generally extracted to avoid complications
We wait for it to pass
questions.explanation: 🦅 Sami explains: 'Luxated baby teeth have a poor prognosis and risk ankylosis.' 🐆 Mina: 'Sami, you're right this time!'

questions.question: 🗣️ Sami, discussing with a parent, says: 'Your 4-year-old child needs orthodontic treatment.' Mina intervenes: 'Not so early!' What is the recommended age for a first orthodontic consultation?
options: Around 7 years for an early evaluation
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Age 7 is recommended for a first orthodontic evaluation.' 🦅 Sami: 'Fine, we'll wait until 7...'

questions.question: 📝 Mina, analyzing an X-ray, says: 'There is a supernumerary tooth.' Sami replies: 'Let's keep it, it's not bothering!' What is the risk with a supernumerary tooth?
options: It can block the eruption of permanent teeth
It does not cause any problems
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Supernumerary teeth can cause eruption delays and crowding.' 🦅 Sami: 'Fine, we'll extract it then...'

questions.question: 🎯 Sami, examining an 8-year-old child, says: 'He has an interproximal cavity.' Mina asks: 'How do you know?' Sami replies: 'I can see it!' What is missing from his diagnosis?
questions.explanation: 🦅 Sami explains: 'Interproximal caries are often clinically invisible, an X-ray is essential.' 🐆 Mina: 'Sami, you're making progress!'

questions.question: 📞 Mina calls Sami: 'I have a 6-year-old child with a baby tooth that has a deep cavity!' Sami replies: 'Pulpotomy!' Mina says: 'And if the cavity is too deep?' What is a pulpectomy?
options: Complete removal of the pulp to treat a deep infection
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Pulpectomy is indicated when pulpotomy is no longer sufficient.' 🦅 Sami: 'I'll remember the difference!'

questions.question: 🏥 Sami and Mina receive a 10-year-old child with a fractured permanent tooth. Sami says: 'Let's extract!' Mina replies: 'We can restore it!' What does the literature say?
options: Coronal fractures can often be restored
questions.explanation: 🦅 Sami explains: 'Uncomplicated coronal fractures can be restored with adhesive materials.' 🐆 Mina: 'Sami, you are really up to date!'

questions.question: 🗣️ Sami, talking to a parent, says: 'Your 3-year-old child has a cavity, it's your fault!' Mina intervenes: 'That's not constructive!' What is the right approach?
options: Explain the causes and solutions without guilt-tripping
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'We must educate and support parents, not judge them.' 🦅 Sami: 'You're right, I'll change my approach.'

questions.question: 📝 Mina, analyzing a case, says: 'The child has enamel hypoplasia.' Sami asks: 'What is that?' What is enamel hypoplasia?
options: A quantitative defect of enamel, often due to a developmental disorder
A tooth that is too large
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Hypoplasia is a defect in enamel formation, often linked to a deficiency or infection.' 🦅 Sami: 'I didn't know that!'

questions.question: 🎯 Sami, examining a 5-year-old child, says: 'He has a Class III malocclusion.' Mina replies: 'Be careful, growth can still change things!' What does growth modify?
options: Mandibular growth can worsen or correct a Class III
questions.explanation: 🦅 Sami explains: 'Mandibular growth is important in the evolution of Class III.' 🐆 Mina: 'Sami, you've understood everything!'

questions.question: 📞 Mina calls Sami: 'I have an 8-year-old child with a persistent baby tooth and the permanent tooth is absent!' Sami replies: 'Let's keep the baby tooth!' What is the strategy?
options: Preserve the baby tooth as a natural space maintainer
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'The baby tooth can serve as a natural space maintainer if the permanent tooth is absent.' 🦅 Sami: 'I didn't think of that, thank you Mina!'

questions.question: 🏥 Sami, in an emergency, sees a 9-year-old child with an avulsed permanent tooth. He says: 'Let's replant it!' Mina asks: 'In what medium?' What is the ideal storage medium?
options: Cold milk, physiological saline, or saliva
questions.explanation: 🦅 Sami explains: 'Cold milk is ideal to preserve periodontal ligament cells.' 🐆 Mina: 'Sami, you're saving teeth!'

questions.question: 🗣️ Sami, discussing with a parent, says: 'Your child must avoid all sugars.' Mina intervenes: 'We should rather manage the frequency.' What is the recommendation?
options: Limit the frequency of sugary intakes (max 4-5 per day)
Allow sugars only in the evening
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'The frequency of sugary intakes is more important than the quantity for caries risk.' 🦅 Sami: 'I'll adapt my advice.'

questions.question: 📝 Mina, analyzing a case, says: 'The child has partial anodontia.' Sami asks: 'What's that?' What is anodontia?
options: The congenital absence of one or more teeth
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Anodontia is a dental agenesis, often of genetic origin.' 🦅 Sami: 'I didn't know this term!'

questions.question: 🎯 Sami, examining a 7-year-old child, says: 'He needs fluoride.' Mina asks: 'In what form?' What are the recommended forms of fluoride?
options: Fluoridated toothpaste, topical fluoride, supplements if deficient
questions.explanation: 🦅 Sami explains: 'The forms vary according to age and caries risk.' 🐆 Mina: 'Sami, you are really complete!'

questions.question: 📞 Mina calls Sami: 'I have a 4-year-old child with severe early childhood caries!' Sami replies: 'Let's extract all the baby teeth!' Mina says: 'And masticatory function?' What is proposed?
options: Nothing, he will eat soft food
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Pediatric crowns preserve function and aesthetics.' 🦅 Sami: 'I'll place crowns then.'

questions.question: 🏥 Sami and Mina receive an 8-year-old child with a baby tooth that won't fall out. Sami says: 'It's a persistent baby tooth!' Mina replies: 'And if it's ankylosis?' What is ankylosis?
options: A fusion of the tooth to the alveolar bone
A tooth that moves too much
questions.explanation: 🦅 Sami explains: 'Ankylosis is a tooth-bone fusion that blocks eruption.' 🐆 Mina: 'Sami, you know your pathologies well!'

questions.question: 🗣️ Sami, talking to a parent, says: 'Your child must stop the pacifier.' Mina intervenes: 'We need to do it gradually.' What is the recommendation?
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'A gradual cessation is more effective and less traumatic.' 🦅 Sami: 'I'll propose a gradual cessation plan.'

questions.question: 📝 Mina, analyzing a complex case, says: 'The child has a baby tooth with internal resorption.' Sami asks: 'What's that?' What is internal resorption?
options: A destruction of the tooth from the inside out
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Internal resorption is a rare pulp pathology.' 🦅 Sami: 'I'll document myself on this subject.'

questions.question: 🤝 Sami and Mina discuss the future of pedodontics. Sami says: 'Parents will manage everything via apps!' Mina replies: 'Human connection remains essential.' What is the future of pediatric care?
options: Technology helps but does not replace the doctor-child-parent relationship
Parents no longer need a dentist
questions.explanation: 🐆 Mina explains: 'Technology is a tool, but human contact is irreplaceable in pedodontics.' 🦅 Sami: 'I agree, we keep our jobs!'
